Kumiho runs a VPN on this phone. While it is connected, the traffic of the apps that use the tunnel goes to a Kumiho proxy server, and that server reaches the sites you asked for. This is what keeps your address away from those sites and what makes the tunnel work.
Android asks for VPN permission in a later step. Nothing is routed until you grant it and connect.
Your Firefox Account tokens are written only to Kumiho\'s private app storage. Android backup and device transfer are turned off for this app, so they are never copied off the phone.
Settings, the server list and the connection logs are local files in the same private storage. A log leaves the phone only when you share it yourself.
There is no telemetry, no analytics and no crash reporting. Nothing is sent to the Kumiho developers.

While the tunnel is up, Kumiho also listens on this phone\'s loopback interface for its local SOCKS5 proxy, and for its local HTTP proxy when you turn that on. Any app on this phone can use them, so treat them as device-wide. Other devices on your network cannot reach them.

Two Android permissions make the tunnel usable. You can finish setup without either of them; Kumiho asks again when you connect.
Android asks you to approve a VPN before any app can carry traffic. Granting it now saves a prompt on your first connect.
Android did not grant the VPN permission. You can still finish setup; Kumiho asks again when you connect.
Kumiho shows a status notification while the tunnel is up, with a Disconnect action. Without it the tunnel still runs; Android just cannot show the status or the action.
Notifications are turned off for Kumiho. You can allow them in Android settings at any time.
Both permissions can be changed later in Android settings.
Android can start Kumiho\'s VPN on its own, including after a reboot. Kumiho never changes this for you: the switch lives in Android\'s VPN settings.
When Always-on VPN is on, Android starts Kumiho whenever no VPN is connected, and Kumiho connects if you are signed in. If you are signed out it asks you to sign in instead of connecting.
Lockdown is stricter: Android blocks all traffic while Kumiho is not connected. Kumiho shows the real state and never works around it.
